signature: Steep, fog-filled hills of even green grass under a constant day, flocks of Shenandoah Sheep drifting through the mist, and all round them a wall of deciduous forest where it is always night and the Nguithr'xurh have strung their silk.

exits.to_label: Any level with heavily forested areas
exits.label: Pushed on into the detritus more than 6 km into the forest and fell through it
exits.source_quote: at any distance greater than 6 km, a traveler will have a 65% chance to no-clip through the detritus
exits.hint: Keep walking away from the light until the litter is deep enough to sink into.

fail_states: lingering beside a Nguithr'xurh sub-cluster in the forest (page: 95% of unaligned travelers do not survive their territory)
entity_policy: SOURCED ENTITIES ONLY: Shenandoah Sheep (grazing flocks in the hills); Nguithr'xurh only in the forest ring, as silk sub-clusters, egg sacs, eye-glints and sound, never seen in the hills and never fought; the Murphy Estate humans are not shown (the page does not place them).
notes: SOURCE: 25 km2 of steep undulating hills and valleys (under 1 m to nearly 80 m, median ~25 m) in a bisected diurnal cycle: constant daylight in the centre, the surrounding dense deciduous forest nightbound; zoysia grass, bluegrass and mosses on loam in uniform growth; one constant condition, fog, densest in valleys and crevices, direction hard to keep; no standing fresh water; ~15,000 Shenandoah Sheep that hydrate from the fog; a Nguithr'xurh super-colony of sub-clusters with queens, highest concentration within 1 km of the border, never in the central area, 95% of unaligned travelers die in it; entrances all occur in the forest ~4 km from the border; exit beyond 6 km in the forest with a 65% chance to no-clip through the detritus into any heavily forested level; Samuel Murphy's 1938 diary names the hills New Shenandoah. ADAPTATION: the hills are scaled to ~0.45 km2 (border radius ~380 m, crests to ~70 m) and forest depth is read at 1 m = 40 m, so the 4 km arrival is 100 m into the trees and the 6 km line is 150 m in; the light, sky and fog blend between day and night with forest depth, and the hills glow with daylight when seen from inside the night; the Nguithr'xurh are shown as silk sheets, funnels, egg sacs and eye-glints (the page's hatchery caption) with clicking sound, and lingering beside a sub-cluster for ~18 s is fatal; each detritus heap beyond 6 km rolls its 65% once when you first reach it; a stone cairn on the highest crest holds the diary page and a wanderer's survey card (paraphrased); a scratched stone at the treeline; the Murphy Estate and the B.N.T.G. trade route are not built because the page keeps them unknown/secret. The streamed forest is a finite window round the player; beyond ~600 m the far forest is a canopy shell. QA mode always opens the authored heap on the arrival bearing and skips threat deaths so the walker bot is deterministic. Canon: docs/canon/levels/L077.md; page by DrAkimoto, CC BY-SA 3.0.
